headline: New managers face 8 harsh realities of leadership
summary: Transitioning from engineer to manager can be challenging
details: Becoming an engineering manager is a challenging and often lonely journey. New managers must learn to manage stress and rumination, and navigate office politics.
A manager's role is different from being part of the team. They must be professional and diplomatic, even when they disagree with a decision.
New managers often feel lonely and miss being an engineer. They must build relationships with colleagues and understand the business to support their teams.

caption:
Are you ready for the 8 harsh realities of leadership?

Becoming an engineering manager is a challenging and often lonely journey. New managers must learn to manage stress and rumination, and navigate office politics.

A manager's role is different from being part of the team. They must be professional and diplomatic, even when they disagree with a decision.

New managers often feel lonely and miss being an engineer. They must build relationships with colleagues and understand the business to support their teams.

Most companies have little to no manager training. New managers are often on their own, learning as they go.
